articles.title: The Gap Strikes Back: Now Stylable
articles.description: Thanks to gap decorations we’ll soon be able to display styled separators between layout items. It looks to be an easy, flexible, and exciting CSS feature that will open up lots of styling possibilities — shown off here via demos and code.
articles.author: Patrick Brosset

articles.title: 🎨 CSS Color Functions
articles.description: Here’s a comprehensive overview of the various color functions and properties now available to us in CSS, including color spaces like sRGB and OKLab, and functions such as rgb(), hsl(), and oklch(). A good way to round out your understanding of the wide array of options in our CSS color toolbox.
articles.author: Sunkanmi Fafowora

articles.title: Introducing Pay Per Crawl: Enabling Content Owners to Charge AI Crawlers for Access
articles.description: Cloudflare has a new, in beta, experimental service which allows AI crawlers to go over a site in exchange for compensation. You can allow, charge, or block. Curious to see where this goes.
articles.author: Allen & Newton (Cloudflare)

articles.title: PNG is Back
articles.description: The PNG spec was recently updated, adding support for HDR, animations, EXIF data, and more. The last time the spec was updated? Over 20 years ago.
articles.author: Chris Blume

articles.title: Understanding CSS corner-shape and the Power of the Superellipse
articles.description: The proposed corner-shape property hopes to expand on the capabilities of border-radius. As it’s an experimental/theoretical property, support is limited to just Chrome Canary — but this post is an interesting introduction as to what may one day be possible: “unlocks a world of new possibilities that previously required complex SVG implementations or image-based solutions”.
articles.author: Amit Sheen

articles.title: ▶  Why Matt Mullenweg Went to 'War' Over WordPress
articles.description: Patel of The Verge speaks with Mullenweg of Automattic on the long, drawn-out saga of WordPress and WPEngine, the future of the web more broadly, and some optimism that AI isn’t going to ‘wreck the web’.
articles.author: Nilay Patel podcast

articles.title: CSS Blob Recipes
articles.description: There’s plenty of blob generators online, but we can also use things like border-radius, the shape() function, or SVGs to achieve a similar look. Juan weighs up the options.
articles.author: Juan Diego Rodríguez

articles.title: Custom Select (That Comes Up From the Bottom on Mobile)
articles.description: Is creating a custom select element that comes up from the bottom better for thumb-reach? Chris tries to find out.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: You're Overthinking Web Components
articles.description: Explores the benefits of using Web Components for progressively enhancing server-rendered HTML, without the need to worry about additional dependencies, the shadow DOM, or going full SPA.
articles.author: Allen Sanford

articles.title: A Step Into the Spatial Web: The HTML Model Element in Apple Vision Pro
articles.description: Admittedly rather niche, but the ability to view 3D models in Apple’s headset directly on the web is pretty neat.
articles.author: Brandel Zachernuk

articles.title: HTML Form Inspector
articles.description: A new, free tool to help audit your forms — just paste in your HTML and it shares an overview of its structure and fields, highlighting any mistakes along with how to fix them.
articles.author: Polypane

articles.title: SVG to CSS Shape Converter: A Simple Tool That Converts SVG Paths to CSS
articles.description: To get it to work, you have to make sure you paste in the value of the d attribute for a single path. Works well, but naturally would take multiple runs to create a full graphic with many paths.
articles.author: Temani Afif

articles.title: FliiipBook: A Simple GIF Animation App for the Web
articles.description: If you've ever messed around with flipbook animation then this will be instantly familiar. Create directly in the browser, and you can download the end result. I had a go at creating a rocket — I can’t draw, but you get the idea. 😄
articles.author: JONATHAN ANDREW MYERS

articles.title: Params Editor: A Chrome Extension to Edit URL Parameters in the Browser
articles.description: Has a comprehensive set of features including expanding long URLs with syntax highlighting, ability to add and customize all sorts of param values, a JSON editor, and more.
articles.author: Utsav Barnwal

articles.title: PicoSSG: A No-Config "Anti-Framework" Static Site Generator
articles.description: Supports Markdown for content and Nunjucks for templating, and boasts a 1:1 file mapping approach that you might find cleaner than other solutions.
articles.author: wolfram kriesing

articles.title: CSV to HTML Table: Display CSV Files as Searchable, Filterable, HTML Tables
articles.description: Not a new project but we haven’t featured it until now. It works by reading a CSV file in a “data” folder and has a simple API to customize the result.
articles.author: Derek Eder
